issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction and conclusion assert that UM-SRD removes unnecessary SRD dissipation in smooth regions, that the blending parameter is near zero in smooth/near-steady regions, that the LTE modification is higher-order in smooth regions, and that the defined choice $s_j=\eta_j^p/(\eta_j^p+\tau^p)$ satisfies the $O(h^p)$ scaling. With the defined indicator $\eta_j=\Delta U_{\max}/(\varepsilon+\Delta U_{\max})$, the paper itself shows $\eta_j\approx 1$ and $s_j\approx 1/(1+\tau^p)\approx 0.99$ whenever any update is nonzero, so in smooth regions UM-SRD coincides with full SRD (confirmed by errors agreeing to 0.01%). The $O(h^p)$ scaling and higher-order LTE result hold only for an unnormalized indicator that is explicitly not the method's definition.

failure_location.quote: SRD continuously applies redistribution even when the flux balance is zero, preventing exact steady-state preservation and introducing unnecessary dissipation in smooth regions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract, introduction and conclusion to claim only exact shut-off when updates vanish, and attribute the $O(h^p)$ scaling and higher-order LTE result explicitly to the unnormalized variant not used in the implementation.

where $W_i$ is the set of neighborhoods contributing to cell $i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is stated for the general weighted-SRD setting with sets $W_i$ and weights $w_{i,j}$ (the conservation constraint $\sum_{j\in W_i}w_{i,j}=1$ is only nontrivial if $|W_i|>1$), but the proof assumes $W_i=\{j\}$ and $w_{i,j}=1$. When a cell belongs to several neighborhoods with different $s_j$, the component formula $U^{n+1}_i=(1-s_j)U^*_i+s_j\sum_k w_{i,k}\hat Q^*_k$ does not specify which $s_j$ to use, and $\sum_i V_i U^{n+1}_i=\sum_i V_iU^*_i$ fails in general because $\sum_k \hat Q^*_k\sum_{i\in M_k} s_{j(i)}w_{i,k}V_i\ne \sum_k s\,\hat V_k\hat Q^*_k$ unless $s$ is constant on each $M_k$. Also per-neighborhood conservation (as stated) is not the right invariant when neighborhoods overlap; only global conservation can hold.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's definition $\tau^{n,base}=B(u^n)-u^{n+1}$ (one-step error, not divided by $\Delta t$), a first-order consistent scheme has $\tau^{n,base}=O(h\Delta t)=O(h^2)$, not $O(h)$. The perturbation $s_j^n(S_j-I)B(u^n)=O(h^{p+1})$ is therefore higher order than the base LTE only for $p>1$; for the admitted value $p=1$ it is the same order $O(h^2)$, so the stated conclusion 'differs ... by a higher-order term' is false at $p=1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the base LTE to $O(h^2)$ and restrict the 'higher-order' conclusion to $p>1$ (or state 'same or higher order' for $p\ge1$).
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's 'higher-order' claim is unsupported at the boundary $p=1$; for $p\ge 2$ the conclusion survives.
issues.title: Local-consistency proposition misidentifies base one-step LTE as $O(h)$; 'higher-order' conclusion fails for $p=1$
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the order bookkeeping and a boundary-case restriction preserve the result for $p\ge 2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary asserts that a one-step truncation-error difference of $O(h)$ (in $\ell^\infty$) is 'the same order as the base first-order scheme' and hence preserves first-order accuracy. The base scheme's one-step LTE is $O(h^2)$, so an $O(h)$ per-step perturbation is one order larger; over $O(1/h)$ steps such a perturbation generically produces $O(1)$ error unless additional damping is proved. No such argument is given, so the conclusion 'UM-SRD with the normalized indicator is still first-order accurate' is unsupported by the proof (the paper itself says a global error estimate is out of scope).

operators directly with $U^* = U$ (zero finite-volume update) for 100

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is posed for 'the 1D model problem with one small cell merged left', where the base scheme is first-order upwind for $u_t+au_x=0$, $a>0$. There $U^*_i=U^n_i$ for all $i$ forces $U^n_i=U^n_{i-1}$ for all $i$ (with $a\Delta t/\Delta x_i>0$), so any steady state is constant and the hypothesis $U^n_{j-1}\ne U^n_j$ can never hold; SRD trivially preserves constant states. The proposition and the corollary about 'smooth steady states $u(x)$' are therefore vacuous in the stated setting, and the introduction's motivating claim of $O(1)$ steady-state drift is not established for the analyzed model. Experiment 6 only tests the redistribution operator with an artificially imposed $U^*=U$ that is not a steady state of the base scheme.
